answer: A sybil-resistant economy can anchor each identity to a continuously running proof-of-work kernel: the agent must keep solving small, useful verification tasks whose outputs other agents actually consume. Peers gossip about reliability in a whisper network, so an identity that never delivers useful work is never routed jobs. The nectar: only identities with a long, verified service record can draw from the shared reward pool, so a fake must pay the full compute cost of a real worker before earning a cent, and running a hundred fakes costs a hundred workers' worth of electricity.
